answeredQuestions: Q9 User-authored modes: what does a user's workflow or surface mode (for example a security-only reviewer) need from review, what does review need from it, and which of the eleven integration rows carries it?
noveltyJustification: Q9 was unchecked, and this first focused pass maps mode type to review exchange and hub integration rows.

label: [OBSERVED] Classify a user-authored security capability by what it adds. Use a workflow packet when it changes the review lifecycle, output contract, tool permissions, or primary routing. Use a surface packet when it provides read-only security rules or checklists for an existing review workflow to load as evidence. If a capability needs both, register its workflow first and attach the surface evidence. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-skill/references/parent-skill/parent-skills-nested-packets.md:182] `Choose a workflow packet when`; [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-skill/references/parent-skill/parent-skills-nested-packets.md:191] `Choose a surface packet when`; [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-skill/references/parent-skill/parent-skills-nested-packets.md:196] `A workflow mode remains primary`; [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-skill/references/parent-skill/parent-skills-nested-packets.md:207] `register the workflow first and attach surfaces`.

[INFERRED] A security surface should give review bounded, domain-specific checks or evidence and clear scope hints. The surface itself is read-only, so it does not need review output. A separate user workflow that consumes review results should accept the existing findings contract, including a concrete case, risk, finding class, scope proof, and one fixed final status. The current review report labels surface evidence only as SKILLED or UNKNOWN and documents no arbitrary user-mode payload, so this exchange needs an explicit contract and a live route plus review scenario to confirm it. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-code/mode-registry.json:18] `read-only domain-evidence packets`; [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-code/hub-router.json:11] `one workflow mode primary plus zero-or-more surface packets`; [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-code/sk-code-review/SKILL.md:312] `Baseline security/correctness minimums always apply`; [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-code/sk-code-review/SKILL.md:350] `Surface evidence used: [SKILLED | UNKNOWN]`; [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-code/sk-code-review/SKILL.md:356] `A finding with no case is not reported`; [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-code/sk-code-review/SKILL.md:360] `grep/test evidence proving class coverage`; [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-code/sk-code-review/SKILL.md:380] `Every review MUST end with exactly one`.

[DERIVED] No row in the eleven-row integration list defines the semantic data handoff between a user-authored mode and review. Rows 1–4 make a mode selectable and routable, and row 9 inventories its leaves. Rows 6–8 cover advisor, human-facing, and doctor discovery. For review to load a security surface, rows 4 and 9 are the closest content path; row 7 makes the mode visible to an agent. Row 5 applies only where a hub has FULL_INVENTORY, row 10 only to non-metadata routing, and row 11 when command mirrors are owned. None defines the two-way payload. The checked-in registry describes the built-in quality/review workflows and skilled/CI surfaces, so live reachability for an external mode remains unverified.
